old: Organic ending ARR growth ~9.2% y/y in Q3 FY2026 (ex ~$480M Semrush), down from ~10.5% in Q2 and 10.9% in Q1; the FY2026 guide implies ~8.3% organic. Reported revenue +12.9% in Q3 includes Semrush.

Competent operator; capital return disciplined. CEO transition on 1 Dec 2026 (Chakravarthy, from Digital Experience/CXO); interim CFO since Q2 FY2026; the FY2026 ARR target of 10.2% was set excluding Semrush (Dec 2025, Mar 2026) and held in June by including Semrush's ~$480M ARR — an organic cut presented as a maintained target.

Shares 475M -> 389M since FY2021; the $20B Figma attempt ended in a $1B fee. SBC 8.0% of revenue. Semrush ($1.87B, closed 28 April 2026, 10-Q Note 3), Topaz Labs (~$340M, agreed 24 June 2026, expected to close in Q4 FY2026), Rilo acquired Sept 2026; management said in Q2 FY2026 it expects more tech tuck-ins. Net cash of $3.76B at FY2023 turned into $1.12B net debt.

Generative AI tools threaten the low end; durability is the open question. Digital Media subscription growth decelerated to +11.2% y/y in Q3 FY2026 (from +13.0% in Q1), while Digital Experience grew ~13% ex-Semrush in each FY2026 quarter, up from ~11% a year earlier (estimate: Adobe does not disclose Semrush revenue; ~$40M in Q2 per the call, ~$120M in Q3 derived from the ~$280M FY2026 guide). The slowdown sits in the creative franchise.

Generative AI substitutes for paid creative seats. Image and video models sold directly by model providers, and browser-first design tools such as Figma, let casual and mid-level users create without Creative Cloud. The early signal is already in the numbers: net new ARR was $400M in Q3 FY2026 against $660M a year earlier (-39%), organic ARR growth is about 9% once Semrush's ~$480M is removed, and management deferred Creative Cloud price increases. Creative and Marketing Professionals is $4.65B of the $6.56B quarterly subscription revenue (71%), so this is the core of the franchise. If revenue growth falls to 3%, the bear case gives $224.80, about today's price.

Leadership turnover during a strategy change. On 1 December 2026 the CEO of 19 years hands over to Anil Chakravarthy, whose background is enterprise marketing software; the CFO left in Q2 FY2026 (interim CFO in place) and the President of Creativity and Productivity is leaving. This happens while the company switches its creative monetization from paywall-first to freemium. Narayen sold 125,000 shares (about $31.3M) on 16–17 September 2026, a week after the announcement, and now holds about $56M of stock (0.06%). A new team can reset targets, change the buyback pace or pursue a large acquisition with no track record to judge it by.

Buybacks and M&A running ahead of free cash flow. Net debt went from -$3,762M at FY2023 to +$1,123M at Q3 FY2026 as $11.3B of FY2025 buybacks and the ~$1.56B Semrush payment exceeded FCF; Topaz Labs is pending. Leverage is still 0.11x EBITDA, so the level is not the problem. The risk is a repeat of the ~$20B Figma attempt (terminated in Q1 FY2024 with a $1B fee): a large acquisition to buy growth would cut the buyback that carries roughly 4 of the 12.9 points of annual EPS growth in the base case.

AI agents take the customer interface at the low end. Intuit is already plugging its software into Perplexity and Meta's Muse agent (August-September 2026), which means the agent, not TurboTax or QuickBooks, may own the first screen the customer sees. DIY is only about 12% of the TurboTax addressable market by management's own count, but it fed more than three quarters of TurboTax Live's customer additions in FY2026. If DIY units keep falling (39.9M to 39.0M in FY2026) the assisted funnel shrinks with them; the Bear case, TurboTax -3% a year and GBS ex-Mailchimp +8%, is worth $234.80 per share.

Credit Karma is a lead-generation business on top of lenders' appetite. It grew 20% to $2,641M in FY2026 (12% of revenue), driven by personal loans, auto insurance and cards, but revenue fell 9.5% in FY2023 when partners cut marketing. A consumer credit downturn inside the three-year window would take the segment below the 10% a year the base case assumes, and QuickBooks Capital adds balance-sheet exposure to small-business loans ($1.9B of loan volume in Q4 FY2026, though an increasing share is sold to forward-flow partners).

Capital allocation and governance. Mailchimp cost about $12B in 2021 (company press release) and now earns about $1.3B of flat revenue (investor day, unverified); its separation into its own segment in FY2027 puts part of the $13,981M of goodwill at risk of impairment. Since 22 January 2026 the CEO also chairs the board, insider selling at $630-680 preceded the fall, and securities class actions allege the company misstated the effect of AI on TurboTax. None is large against a $71.6B market cap, but together they reduce the margin for trust in management's reset.

AI lowers the cost of writing vertical software, and the recurring base starts to leak. 75.6% of LTM revenue ($9,557M) is maintenance and recurring fees whose value rests on switching costs; if challengers or customers' own tools make switching cheaper, price increases stop sticking before customers leave. Maintenance organic growth already slowed to 2% in Q2 FY2026 (4% ex-Altera) from 5–6% historically. Each point of lost organic growth on the recurring base is about $95M of revenue a year, and at the bear case (1% maintenance, -1% total) FY2029 FCFA2S is $2,160M instead of $2,850M, C$2,225 per share instead of C$4,241. The portfolio cannot be screened for exposure from outside: management itself will not classify it by AI risk.

Capital allocation drifts after the founder. Mark Leonard resigned in September 2025 and left the board in May 2026; he set the hurdle-rate culture that made reinvestment work. Under Mark Miller deployment accelerated to $1,702M of total consideration in H1 FY2026, with larger deals at higher prices (DerbySoft ~$400M, bought at a multiple the CFO called high, partly with leverage) and the 2026 cohort at a 16% margin in Q2 FY2026 against the high 20s to 30s of mature cohorts. If new capital earns 12% instead of the ~20%+ implied by history, FCFA2S per share compounds at single digits and the stock deserves the bear multiple (6.5% yield). The damage would show slowly, a cohort at a time.

Consolidated figures overstate what belongs to CSU shareholders. Topicus and Lumine are consolidated at 100%, but CSU owns 61.4% of Lumine and a minority economic stake in Topicus; minorities hold $744M of equity, took $29M of $303M of Q2 FY2026 net income, and $2,724M of debt sits in subsidiaries without recourse to CSU. On top, the IRGA liability ($1,186M at Q2 FY2026, about C$79 per share) is a put held by Topicus minorities (Joday and others) that CSU may have to settle in cash; it is revalued every quarter and is not deducted in the base case. If FCFA2S is not already net of the minorities' share, attributable FCFA2S is roughly 10% lower (hypothesis) and so is the target.

Management held the FY2026 target of 10.2% ending ARR growth on the $25.66B opening book, which means $28.28B at year end and about $780M of net new ARR in Q4, against $400M in Q3 and $920M in Q4 FY2025. Q4 is the seasonal enterprise quarter. Hitting it says the freemium push is costing growth only at the margin; missing it says the Q3 slowdown (-39% y/y net new ARR) is the trend.

Tiers (assume Semrush ARR flat at $480M; Q3 ARR $27.5B, rounded): Q4 net new ARR < ~$690M → FY26 organic ARR growth < 8% (claim 1 breached); < ~$440M → organic < 7% (break k1 fires). Hitting the guide (~$780M) still counts as strike 1 of k1's net-new leg (below $920M of Q4 FY2025). If Adobe discloses Semrush ARR, recompute organic with the disclosed figure.

Measurement note (k1): Adobe revalues the ARR book at new FX rates at the start of each fiscal year. The k1 net-new comparison for Q1 FY2027 against the $400M of Q1 FY2026 must use the same FX basis: restate the FY2026 figure at FY2027 rates if Adobe discloses it.

RPO has been flat for three quarters ($22.52B, $22.22B, $22.27B, $22.16B) and grew 8% y/y in Q3, the first single-digit print since early FY2023. Management says RPO always steps up in Q4 and stays flat for three quarters (Q4 FY2025 added $2.08B). A weak step-up would confirm that enterprise and multi-year commitments are slowing along with ARR.

Q1 FY2027 (reported around 19 November 2026) is the first print with Mailchimp reported separately. Management guided GBS to 13-14% for the year and total company revenue to about 11% for the quarter.

GBS ex-Mailchimp grew about 17-18% in FY2026. A first quarter already at the low end of the range would say the online core is slowing faster than the base case's 12% a year allows, and that the low end is not only a TurboTax problem.

Federal units fell from 39.9M to 39.0M in FY2026, and management chose to cut DIY prices to win them back, accepting lower ARPC. The FY2027 guide assumes flat IRS filers and TurboTax revenue growth of only 2-3%.

If the price reset brings units back to growth, the DIY loss was pricing, which Intuit controls. If units fall again at lower prices, the substitute is structural and the Bear case gains weight. Known with Q3 FY2027 results in May 2027.

The 17% workforce reduction (announced 20 May 2026, about $300M of restructuring charges) is meant to fund more sales and marketing and product spend while still expanding margin. The FY2027 GAAP EPS guide of $20.12-20.36 at a 27% tax rate implies a GAAP operating margin of roughly 31-32%, against 27.4% in FY2026.

The base case needs 33% by FY2029. If the price and acquisition push absorbs the savings, the margin leg of the thesis breaks.

Q2 FY2026 printed 2% maintenance and recurring organic growth (FX-adjusted), 4% ex-Altera, the weakest in the eight quarters on record. The CFO blamed prior-year comps at Altera and Dark Matter, a South American customer loss (~30bps) and Lumine turnarounds, and said growth should normalise toward 5% based on what CSU owns today.

If Q3 FY2026 comes back to 4% or more, the moat reading holds and the AI discount has less to stand on. If it stays at 2–3%, the one-off explanation weakens and the base case's 3.5% looks generous.

The December call is Anil Chakravarthy's first set of annual targets. The base case needs revenue to compound at 7% and GAAP operating margin to hold at 35% (non-GAAP about 45% in FY2026). A reset year, with growth guided down to mid-single digits or margin cut to fund AI, would move us toward the bear case. A target that includes Topaz repeats the Semrush pattern: inorganic ARR holding a headline number.

Dan Durn left in Q2 FY2026 and Steve Day is interim CFO; David Wadhwani is also leaving. The thesis leans on the buyback ($2.23B in Q3 FY2026, $9.3B LTM, $24.55B authorization left). A permanent CFO and an unchanged repurchase pace would say capital allocation survives the handover; a pause, or a large acquisition, would not.

Intuit repurchased $6,121M of stock in FY2026 (cash flow statement), $2,205M of it in Q4, and said repurchases will remain a significant part of capital allocation in FY2027. At $268, one quarter at that pace (about $1,530M) retires about 2% of the shares, gross of SBC dilution.

The base case needs diluted shares to fall about 3% a year, to 250M by FY2029. A quarter below $1,500M, with net debt still near $1.1B, would say the company is protecting the balance sheet ahead of something.

Total consideration was $809M in Q1 FY2026 and $893M in Q2 FY2026, and the company disclosed another $818M closed or committed early in Q3 (press reports of the Q2 release): about $2.52B already visible against $1,579M for all of FY2025.

Crossing $2.5B for the year shows the post-Leonard team can put FCFA2S to work at its hurdle rates, which is the whole of pillar 3. The base case needs about $2.7B a year of cash spend.

The CFO gave cohort margins on the Q2 FY2026 call: the 2026 cohort went from -16% in Q1 to +16% in Q2, the 2025 cohort from 16–17% to about 20%, while older cohorts run in the high 20s to 30s. DerbySoft (~$400M) was bought at a multiple the CFO called high and partly funded with leverage.

If the 2025 and 2026 cohorts are still below 20% when management next discusses them (Q4 FY2026 call, March 2027), the acceleration in deployment is buying lower returns, and the base case's 15% FCFA2S margin is at risk.

On the Q1 FY2026 call the CFO said CSU is discussing whether to give investors the "economic net income" measure used internally for bonuses, because FCFA2S does not capture its pro-rata share of minority investments (PEMs, e.g. the Asseco Poland stake). A new metric would change how the market and this model anchor value.

Neutral by itself; it matters for the valuation basis. If it lands, the base case should be re-run on the new measure and reconciled to FCFA2S.

Adobe trades at 13.0x LTM GAAP EPS of $17.92 and about 9.5x the FY2026 non-GAAP EPS guide of $24.45–24.50, at $233 against a $360 high in October 2025. The market is pricing generative AI as a substitute for Creative Cloud and Acrobat seats. The numbers so far show a slower franchise, not a shrinking one: revenue grew at a 10.5% 3Y CAGR to $23.8B in FY2025 and 12.9% y/y in Q3 FY2026, gross margin is 89%, GAAP operating margin is 35.7% LTM and ROIC 35%. What is slowing is the rate of new ARR: $400M net new in Q3 FY2026, down 39% y/y, while management defers price increases and pushes a freemium funnel (Creative freemium MAU >100M, +70% y/y). The thesis buys a subscription franchise at a multiple that assumes decline.

Valuation is 15x FY2029 GAAP EPS, not non-GAAP, so stock-based compensation (8.0% of revenue) is treated as a cost. Revenue compounds at 7% from the $26.6B FY2026 guide midpoint to $32.6B, below the 10.5% 3Y CAGR and below the ~9% organic ARR growth of Q3 FY2026 (reported 11.2% includes $480M of Semrush ARR). GAAP operating margin holds at 35%, tax at 22%, and shares fall from 389M to 345M. That gives $25.79 of EPS and $387 per share. The multiple moves from 13x to 15x, still well below the 19x of FY2025 year end; most of the return comes from EPS growth and a smaller share count. At 11x on $20 of EPS (3% growth, 32% margin) the bear case lands at $225, close to today's price.

The return engine is the buyback. LTM free cash flow was $10.6B (40.8% margin, 1.45x net income, capex 0.8% of revenue) and $9.3B went to repurchases; period-end shares fell 6.9% y/y to 391M in Q3 FY2026, and $24.55B remains under the April 2026 authorization. At an 11.7% FCF yield (8.6x FCF), every year of buybacks at this price retires more stock than the same dollars would at the 2021–2024 multiples. The second leg is AI monetization inside the installed base: AI-first ending ARR above $650M (+150% y/y), Firefly ARR +40% q/q, and AEM, GenStudio and AEP each growing ARR above 20%. The engine only works if FCF holds near $10B and management does not redirect it to a large acquisition.

Organic ending ARR growth (excluding the ~$480M of Semrush ARR and any Topaz ARR) falls below 7% y/y, or net new ARR declines y/y for two more consecutive quarters after Q3 FY2026 (Q4 FY2026 below the $920M of Q4 FY2025 counts as the first). FY2026 guidance already implies ~$780M in Q4.

LTM GAAP operating margin falls below 33% (35.7% today), or the FY2027 non-GAAP operating margin target comes in below 42% (about 45% for FY2026, 44% guided for Q4 FY2026), which would mean AI compute and freemium costs are eating the margin rather than being funded by growth.

Period-end diluted share count shrinks less than 2% y/y, LTM FCF drops below $9B, or Adobe announces an acquisition above $5B funded with debt that pushes net debt/EBITDA above 1.0x (0.11x today). The 2022 attempt to buy Figma for about $20B, terminated with a $1B fee in Q1 FY2024, is the precedent.

CSU is the permanent owner of about 1,300 small vertical market software businesses in 140 verticals (FY2025, FiscalAI KPIs), each selling mission-critical software to a narrow customer set: transit agencies, utilities, clubs, dealers, hospitals. 75.6% of LTM revenue ($9,557M of $12,641M) is maintenance and other recurring revenue, which grew organically 5–6% a year FX-adjusted from FY2022 to FY2025 while licences shrank. The units are not integrated; head office allocates capital and holds managers to hurdle rates. You are buying two things: an annuity of recurring fees with low churn, and a reinvestment engine that took FCFA2S from $853M in FY2022 to $1,683M in FY2025 (25% 3Y CAGR) with no new shares (21.19M since FY2021). The stock fell from C$4,993 (30 Jun 2025) to C$2,896 (29 Sep 2026) on two events: fear that AI erodes VMS pricing and switching costs, and founder Mark Leonard's resignation for health reasons in September 2025.

Valuation is on FCFA2S (free cash flow available to shareholders: CFO less interest, lease payments and capex), the company's own yardstick, not on reported EPS, which is distorted by amortisation of acquired intangibles ($1,383M of D&A in FY2025) and the quarterly revaluation of the IRGA put liability owed to Topicus minorities. LTM FCFA2S is $2,030M, $95.80 per share, or C$135.9 at 1.419 CAD per USD: a 4.7% yield (21.3x) at C$2,896. At fiscal year-ends FY2023–FY2025 the stock traded on a 2.6% average yield (40x). The base case pays 4.5% (22.2x) for FY2029 FCFA2S of $2,850M: $19.0B of revenue from ~2% organic growth plus acquisitions, at a 15.0% FCFA2S margin against a 14.3% 3Y average. That is C$4,241 per share, +46%. No re-rating is assumed; the multiple stays near today's level, so the return has to come from compounding FCFA2S per share.

The return comes from reinvestment, not payouts. CSU pays $85M a year in dividends and does not buy back stock; the rest of FCFA2S goes into acquisitions at hurdle rates management says have not changed (Q2 FY2026 call). Deployment re-accelerated after a slow FY2025 ($1,340M cash, $1,579M total consideration): $809M of total consideration in Q1 FY2026 and $893M in Q2 FY2026, plus $818M closed or committed early in Q3 (press reports of the Q2 release). LTM cash spent on acquisitions ($2,228M) exceeds LTM FCFA2S ($2,030M), a 110% reinvestment rate. If that capital earns returns close to the historical record while recurring revenue keeps growing organically, FCFA2S per share compounds in the low-to-mid teens without dilution. The pressure point is price: larger deals such as DerbySoft (~$400M) come at higher multiples, and the 2026 acquisition cohort ran at a 16% margin in Q2 FY2026 against the high 20s to 30s of mature cohorts (CFO, Q2 FY2026 call).

Total maintenance and recurring organic growth (FX-adjusted) below 2% for two consecutive quarters from Q3 FY2026 onward, once the Altera and Dark Matter prior-year comps lapse, or any disclosure of AI-related customer attrition. Q2 FY2026 printed 2% (4% ex-Altera).
LTM FCFA2S margin below 13.5% (3Y average 14.3%, LTM 16.1%), or FCFA2S per share growing less than 8% a year through FY2027. That path leads to the bear case of C$2,225.

Cash spent on acquisitions below $1.5B in FY2027, or the 2025 and 2026 cohorts still below a 20% margin by Q4 FY2027 (CFO: 2025 cohort ~20%, 2026 cohort 16% in Q2 FY2026), or a turn to buybacks or special dividends that signals deals at hurdle cannot be found.

Intuit is two platforms. The business platform (Global Business Solutions: QuickBooks online and desktop, payroll, payments, capital, Mailchimp) made $12,864M in FY2026, +16%; its online ecosystem made $9,918M, +19%. The consumer platform (TurboTax $5,296M, Credit Karma $2,641M, ProTax $647M) made $8,584M, +11%. The stock fell from $683 (October 2025) to $268 because the market reads AI agents and cheap filers as the end of paid DIY tax and low-end bookkeeping. The low end is under real pressure: TurboTax federal units fell 2.3% to 39.0M and online paying customers grew only 3%. The core is not: online ecosystem ARPC grew 15%, mid-market revenue 39%, online payment volume 30% to $225B, and Credit Karma 20%. The thesis buys the ledger and tax data of millions of US small businesses and filers, plus the accountant network around them, where switching costs and compliance liability matter more than the interface.

Valued on GAAP EPS, which already carries stock-based compensation ($2,056M in FY2026, 9.6% of revenue); from FY2027 the company's non-GAAP figures include it too. At $268 the stock trades at 16.3x FY2026 EPS of $16.46 and 13.2x the $20.24 midpoint of FY2027 GAAP EPS guidance, with a 12.1% FCF yield ($8,663M), or 9.2% after subtracting SBC. The base case applies 18x to FY2029 EPS of $26.60: revenue of $27.5B (8.7% a year, below the 9-10% FY2027 guide), GAAP EBIT margin of 33% against 27.4% in FY2026 and roughly 31.7% implied by the FY2027 guide, and 250M diluted shares. That gives $479 per share. 18x sits far below the 3-year average of 46x; the case needs no return to software multiples, only a move from 13x forward earnings to a mature compounder multiple.

The return comes from earnings growth of about 16% a year plus a share count that shrinks. In FY2026 Intuit spent $6,121M on buybacks and $1,347M on dividends out of $8,663M of FCF, and period-end shares fell 3.8%, from 279.1M to 268.4M. At today's price, a year of buybacks at that pace retires about 8% of the company. Margin support is already decided: a 17% workforce reduction announced in May 2026, and SBC guided down to 8% of revenue by FY2030. Net debt is $1,136M including leases, 0.17x EBITDA, so the buyback does not need leverage. What the thesis does not assume is a reacceleration: the new-customer push (QuickBooks Free and Lite, lower DIY tax prices) is upside if it works, and the base case already absorbs the lower tax ARPC it costs.

Online ecosystem revenue growth (excluding Mailchimp) below 12% year over year for two consecutive quarters, online paying customers falling year over year, or TurboTax federal units below 39.0M again in the 2027 season after the price cuts.

FY2027 GAAP EPS below the $20.12 low end of guidance, FY2027 GAAP operating margin below 30%, or the DIY price cuts spreading into assisted tax (TurboTax Live revenue growth below 10% in FY2027 against a mid-teens guide).
FY2027 weighted diluted shares above 271M (less than 2% below the 277M of FY2026), net debt above 1x EBITDA to fund repurchases, or FCF minus SBC below $6,000M.
$28.28B FY2026 exit compounded at 3%: generative tools substitute for entry and mid-tier Creative Cloud seats and net new ARR keeps falling, as it did in Q3 FY2026 (-39% y/y).

389M to 355M, -3.0% a year. Hypothesis: with the franchise under pressure, management diverts cash to acquisitions to buy growth (precedent: Figma at about $20B in 2022), so the share count falls less than the cheap price would allow.

389M to 345M, a net reduction of about 3.9% a year against 6.9% over the last twelve months. Slower than today because a higher price buys fewer shares and part of FCF goes to M&A (Semrush $1.56B in Q2 FY2026, Topaz Labs pending).
$8,896M over 345M shares. Against $17.92 LTM that is a 12.9% annual growth rate, of which about 4 points come from the share count. The FY2026 GAAP guide is $18.12–18.17.

FY2026 guide of 10.2% on $25.66B gives $28.28B at year end, compounded at 7% to $34.64B in FY2029. Reported Q3 FY2026 growth is 11.2%, but ~9% organic after the ~$480M of Semrush ARR. History is Digital Media ARR, FY2022 $13.26B to FY2025 $19.20B (13.1% CAGR), used as a proxy because total ARR is only disclosed from FY2023.

$26.6B FY2026 guide midpoint compounded at 7% for three years. Below the 10.5% 3Y CAGR (FY2022 $17.6B to FY2025 $23.8B) because net new ARR fell 39% y/y in Q3 FY2026 and price increases were deferred.

Held near the 35.7% LTM and above the 34.1% FY2023–FY2025 average (FY2024 carried the $1B Figma termination fee). No operating leverage assumed: AI compute and freemium costs absorb it. Non-GAAP margin was 44.0% in Q3 FY2026 against 46.3% a year earlier.
GAAP tax rate guided at about 22.5% for FY2026; LTM 21.5%, FY2023–FY2025 average 19.5%. Net non-operating income is taken as zero: LTM interest expense of $260M is offset by interest income on cash.

15x GAAP EPS, from 13.0x today. Below the 19.2x at FY2025 year end and far below the 3Y average of 37.6x (FY2023–FY2025 year-end prices), which belonged to a faster-growing Adobe. On non-GAAP EPS this would be roughly 11x.

Held at the Q3 FY2026 $1,123M (debt $6,762M including $399M of leases, less $5,639M cash and short-term investments): buybacks absorb FCF. History is the FY2023–FY2025 average of -$1,846M, per house rule.
Net income times 1.35, below the 1.45x LTM conversion because SBC growth is assumed to slow. A 9.0% FCF yield on the target market cap, against 11.7% today.

GBS excluding Mailchimp (about $11,564M) grows 12% a year to $16,247M, the middle of management's 10-15% three-year range and below the 13-14% FY2027 guide; Mailchimp flat at about $1,300M (unverified). History: $8,038M in FY2023 to $12,864M in FY2026, a 3Y CAGR of 17.0% (FiscalAI).

+3% a year, the top of the 2-3% FY2027 guide held for three years: lower DIY prices offset by TurboTax Live growth. History: $4,508M in FY2024 to $5,296M in FY2026, +8.4% a year (only two years on the current segment basis). Federal units fell from 39.9M to 39.0M in FY2026.
+10% a year, below the 11-13% FY2027 guide because partner lending demand is cyclical. History: $1,634M in FY2023 to $2,641M in FY2026, a 3Y CAGR of 17.4% off a trough; it fell 9.5% in FY2023.

27.4% in FY2026, 28.8% before the $293M restructuring charge; the FY2027 GAAP EPS guide implies roughly 31-32%. 33% by FY2029 adds about 65bps a year after that, helped by the 17% workforce cut and SBC falling toward 8% of revenue. 3Y average 25.3%.

From 277M weighted diluted in FY2026 (267.2M outstanding today) to 250M, about 3% a year net of SBC. FY2026 buybacks of $6,121M cut period-end shares 3.8%. The 3Y CAGR of -0.7% reflects years when buybacks only offset dilution.

$6,650M over 250M shares. 14.6% a year from the $20.24 FY2027 guide midpoint and 17.3% a year from FY2026's $16.46. GAAP includes SBC and $659M of acquired-intangible amortization, so it is the conservative earnings line. History: $8.42 in FY2023, 3Y CAGR 25.0%.

18x on FY2029 GAAP EPS. The stock trades at 16.3x LTM and 13.2x the FY2027 guide; the 3Y average of 46.2x (62.1x, 57.4x, 19.2x at fiscal year ends) belongs to a growth regime the case does not assume back.
Falls out of the P/E chain: $120.8B EV ($119.7B market cap plus about $1.1B of net debt) on $9,987M of EBITDA. 10.8x today; 3Y average 31.0x.

Held roughly flat: the company returns about all of FCF through buybacks and dividends and refinances maturities. $1,136M at 4Q FY2026 including $667M of leases. History is the 3-year average per house rule: $2,422M (FY2024), $2,018M (FY2025), $1,136M (FY2026), average $1,859M.
